paragraphs.sourceText: There're three main types of financial stress people encounter. The first type is apparent in people being stressed about the 26 ups and downs of investment markets-actually not so much the ups, but 27 the downs. These people are usually unable or unprepared to endure the long haul.

The next common type of financial stress is that caused by debt. In a 28 percentage of cases of debt-induced financial stress, credit cards and loans will be a central element. Often there'll be a car loan and perhaps a mortgage, but credit cards often seem to be the gateway to debt-related financial difficulties for many.
The third type of stress and 29 the least known is inherited financial stress, which is the most destructive. It is experienced by those who have grown up in households where their parents regularly
30 and fought about money. Money therefore becomes a stressful topic, and so the thought of sitting down and planning is an unattractive 31

Those suffering inherited financial anxiety 32 to follow one of two patterns. Either they put their head in the sand, they would 33 examining their financial statements, budgeting, and discussing financial matters with those closest to them. Alternatively, they would go to the other
34 , and micro-analyze everything, to the point of complete 35 . They're convinced that whatever decision they make will be the wrong one.

paragraphs.sourceText: Doctor's orders: Let children just play
paragraphs.translationZh: 医生嘱咐：让孩子尽情玩耍

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Imagine a drug that could enhance a child's creativity and critical thinking. Imagine that this drug were simple to make, safe to take, and could be had for free. The nation's leading pediatricians (儿科医生) say this miracle compound exists. In a new clinical report, they are urging doctors to prescribe it liberally to the children in their care.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 想象一种可以增强孩子创造力和批判性思维的药物。想象一下这种药物制作简单、服用安全并且可以免费获得。美国领先的儿科医生表示这种神奇的化合物是存在的。在一份新的临床报告中，他们敦促医生为他们照顾的孩子慷慨地开药。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) "This may seem old-fashioned, but there are skills to be learned when kids aren't told what to do," said Dr. Michael Yogman, a Harvard Medical School pediatrician who led the drafting of the call to arms. Whether it's rough physical play, outdoor play or pretend play, kids derive important lessons from the chance to make things up as they go, he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）“这可能看起来很过时，但是当孩子们不被告知该做什么时，可以学习一些技能，”哈佛医学院儿科医生迈克尔·约格曼博士说，他领导了战斗呼吁的起草。他说，无论是粗暴的体力游戏、户外游戏还是假装游戏，孩子们都能从边玩边编的机会中学到重要的教训。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) The advice, issued Monday by the American Academy of Pediatrics, may come as a shock to some parents. After spending years fretting (烦恼) over which toys to buy, which apps to download and which skill-building programs to send their kids to after school, letting them simply play-or better yet, playing with them-could seem like a step backward. The pediatricians insist that it's not. The academy's guidance does not include specific recommendations for the dosing of play. Instead, it asks doctors to advise parents before their babies turn two that play is essential to healthy development.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 美国儿科学会周一发布的建议可能会让一些家长感到震惊。在花了数年时间为买哪些玩具、下载哪些应用程序以及放学后送孩子参加哪些技能培养项目而烦恼（烦恼）之后，让他们简单地玩耍——或者更好的是，和他们一起玩——似乎是一种倒退。儿科医生坚称事实并非如此。该学院的指导不包括有关比赛剂量的具体建议。相反，它要求医生在婴儿两岁之前建议父母，玩耍对于健康发育至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) "Play is not silly behavior," the academy's report declares. It fosters children's creativity, cooperation, and problem-solving skills-all of which are critical for a 2lst-century workforce. When parents engage in play with their children, it builds a wall against the harmful effects of all kinds of stress, including poverty, the academy says. In the pediatricians' view, essentially every life skill that's valued in adults can be built up with play. "Collaboration, negotiation, decision-making, creativity, leadership, and increased physical activity are just some of the skills and benefits children gain through play," they wrote. The pediatricians' appeal comes as kids are being squeezed by increasing academic demands at school and the constant invasion of digital media.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）“玩耍不是愚蠢的行为，”该学院的报告宣称。它培养孩子的创造力、合作能力和解决问题的能力——所有这些对于 2 世纪的劳动力都至关重要。该学院表示，当父母与孩子一起玩耍时，就会筑起一道墙，抵御包括贫困在内的各种压力的有害影响。在儿科医生看来，基本上成年人重视的每一项生活技能都可以通过玩耍来培养。他们写道：“合作、谈判、决策、创造力、领导力和增加体育活动只是孩子们通过玩耍获得的一些技能和好处。”儿科医生的吸引力之际，孩子们正受到学校日益增长的学术要求和数字媒体的不断入侵的挤压。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The trends have been a long time coming. Between 1981 and 1997, detailed time-use studies showed that the time children spent at play declined by 25 percent. Since the adoption of sweeping education reforms in 2001, public schools have steadily increased the amount of time devoted to preparing for standardized tests. The focus on academic "skills and drills" has cut deeply into recess (课间休息) and other time for free play.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 这种趋势已经出现很长时间了。 1981 年至 1997 年间，详细的时间使用研究表明，孩子们花在玩耍上的时间减少了 25%。自2001年实行全面的教育改革以来，公立学校稳步增加了准备标准化考试的时间。对学术“技能和训练”的关注已经深深地占用了课间休息和其他自由活动的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) By 2009, a study of Los Angeles kindergarten classrooms found that five-year-olds were so burdened with academic requirements that they were down to an average of just 19 minutes per day of "choice time," when they were permitted to play freely with blocks, toys or other children. One in four Los Angeles teachers reported there was no time at all for "free play." Increased academic pressures have left 30 percent of U.S. kindergarten classes without any recess. Such findings prompted the American Academy of Pediatrics to issue a policy statement in 2013 on the "crucial role of recess in school."
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 到 2009 年，一项针对洛杉矶幼儿园教室的研究发现，5 岁的孩子在学业要求上负担过重，以至于每天平均只有 19 分钟的“选择时间”，因为他们被允许自由地玩积木、玩具或其他孩子。四分之一的洛杉矶教师表示根本没有时间“自由玩耍”。学业压力的增加导致美国幼儿园 30% 的课程没有课间休息。这些发现促使美国儿科学会于 2013 年发布了一份关于“课间休息在学校中的关键作用”的政策声明。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Pediatricians aren't the only ones who have noticed. Tn a report titled "Crisis in the Kindergarten," a group of educators, health professionals and child advocates called the loss of play in early childhood ''a tragedy, both for the children themselves and for our nation and the world." Kids in play-based kindergartens "end up equally good or better at reading and other intellectual skills, and they are more likely to become well-adjusted healthy people," the Alliance for Childhood said in 2009. Indeed, new research demonstrates why playing with blocks might have been time better spent, Yogman said. The trial assessed the effectiveness of an early mathematics intervention ( -tffii) aimed at preschoolers. The results showed almost no gains in math achievement.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 儿科医生并不是唯一注意到这一点的人。在一份题为《幼儿园危机》的报告中，一群教育工作者、卫生专业人员和儿童权益倡导者称，儿童早期失去游戏“对孩子们自己、对我们的国家和世界来说都是一场悲剧。”儿童联盟在 2009 年表示，以游戏为基础的幼儿园的孩子“最终在阅读和其他智力技能方面同样优秀甚至更好，而且他们更有可能成为适应良好的健康人”。约格曼说，这项试验评估了针对学龄前儿童的早期数学干预（-tffii）的有效性，结果显示数学成绩几乎没有提高。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Another playtime thief: the growing proportion of kids' time spent in front of screens and digital devices, even among preschoolers. Last year, Common Sense Media reported that children up through age eight spent an average of two hours and 19 minutes in front of screens each day, including an average of 42 minutes a day for those under two. This increase of digital use comes with rising risks of obesity, sleep deprivation and cognitive (认知的) , language and social-emotional delays, the American Academy of Pediatrics warned in 2016.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 另一个游戏时间小偷：孩子们花在屏幕和数字设备前的时间比例越来越大，甚至在学龄前儿童中也是如此。去年，Common Sense Media 报道称，8 岁以上的儿童每天平均在屏幕前花费 2 小时 19 分钟，其中两岁以下的儿童平均每天花 42 分钟。美国儿科学会在 2016 年警告说，数字化使用的增加伴随着肥胖、睡眠不足以及认知、语言和社交情感迟缓的风险上升。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) "I respect that parents have busy lives and it's easy to hand a child an iPhone," Yogman said. "But there's a cost to that. For young children, it's much too passive. And kids really learn better when they're actively engaged and have to really discover things."
paragraphs.translationZh: I) “我尊重父母忙碌的生活，给孩子一部 iPhone 很容易，”约格曼说。 “但这也是有代价的。对于年幼的孩子来说，这太被动了。当孩子们积极参与并真正发现事物时，他们真的会学得更好。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The decline of play is a special hazard for the roughly 1 in 5 children in the United States who live in poverty. These 14 million children most urgently need to develop the resilience (韧劲) that is cultivated with play. Instead, Yogman said, they are disproportionately affected by some of the trends that are making play scarce: academic pressures at schools that need to improve test scores, outside play areas that are limited or unsafe, and parents who lack the time or energy to share in playtime.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 对于美国大约五分之一的贫困儿童来说，玩耍的减少是一个特殊的危险。这 1400 万儿童最迫切需要培养通过玩耍培养的韧性。约格曼说，相反，他们受到一些导致游戏稀缺的趋势的影响：学校需要提高考试成绩的学业压力，有限或不安全的户外游戏区域，以及父母缺乏时间或精力分享游戏时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Yogman also worries about the pressures that squeeze playtime for more affluent kids. "The notion that as parents we need to schedule every minute of their time is not doing them a great service," he said. Even well-meaning parents may be "robbing them of the opportunity to have that joy of discovery and curiosity-the opportunity to find things out on their own. "
paragraphs.translationZh: K) Yogman 还担心富裕孩子玩耍时间受到挤压的压力。 “作为父母，我们需要安排好他们每一分钟的时间，这对他们来说并没有什么好处，”他说。即使是善意的父母也可能“剥夺了他们享受发现和好奇心的乐趣——自己发现事物的机会。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Play may not be a hard sell to kids. But UCLA pediatrician Carlos Lerner acknowledged that the pediatricians' new prescription may meet with skepticism OZ-iit.) from parents, who are anxious for advice on how to give their kids a leg up in the world. They should welcome the simplicity of the message, Lerner said. "It's liberating to be able to offer them this advice: that you spending time with your child and letting him play is one of the most valuable things you can do," he said. "It doesn't have to involve spending a lot of money or time, or joining a parenting group. It's something we can offer that's achievable. They just don't recognize it right now as particularly valuable."
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 对于孩子们来说，玩耍可能并不难。但加州大学洛杉矶分校的儿科医生卡洛斯·勒纳承认，儿科医生的新处方可能会遭到父母的怀疑，他们急于寻求如何让孩子在世界上站稳脚跟的建议。勒纳说，他们应该欢迎这种简单的信息。 “能够向他们提供这样的建议是一种解放：花时间陪伴孩子并让他玩耍是你能做的最有价值的事情之一，”他说。 “这并不需要花费大量金钱或时间，或者加入育儿团体。这是我们可以提供的、可以实现的东西。他们只是现在不认为它特别有价值。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Increased use of digital devices steals away children's playtime.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 越来越多地使用数字设备夺走了孩子们的玩耍时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Since the beginning of this century, an increasing amount of time has been shifted in public schools from recess to academic activities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 自本世纪初以来，公立学校越来越多的时间从课间休息转移到学术活动上。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. It has been acknowledged that while kids may welcome pediatricians' recommendation, their parents may doubt its feasibility.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 人们承认，虽然孩子们可能会欢迎儿科医生的建议，但家长可能会怀疑其可行性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. According to some professionals, deprivation of young children's playtime will do harm not only to children themselves but to the country and the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 一些专业人士认为，剥夺幼儿的游戏时间不仅会危害儿童本身，还会危害国家和世界。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. By playing with children, parents can prevent them from being harmed by stress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.通过与孩子玩耍，父母可以防止他们受到压力的伤害。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Playing with digital devices discourages kids from active discovery, according to pediatrician
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 儿科医生表示，玩数字设备会阻碍孩子主动发现

paragraphs.sourceText: Dr. Michael Yogman.
paragraphs.translationZh: 迈克尔·约格曼博士。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The suggestion of letting children simply play may sound like going backwards to parents who want to help build their children's skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 让孩子们简单地玩耍的建议对于那些想要帮助培养孩子技能的父母来说可能听起来像是一种倒退。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Dr. Michael Yogman believes the idea that parents should carefully schedule children's time may not be helpful to their growth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. Michael Yogman博士认为，父母应该仔细安排孩子的时间的想法可能对他们的成长没有帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. One quarter of teachers in an American city said that children in kindergartens had no time for playing freely.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 美国某城市四分之一的教师表示，幼儿园的孩子没有时间自由玩耍。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to a pediatrician, no matter what kind of play children engage in, they are learning how to create things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 根据儿科医生的说法，无论孩子们玩什么游戏，他们都在学习如何创造东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Americans spend billions of dollars each year trying to change their weight with diets, gym memberships and plastic surgery.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国人每年花费数十亿美元试图通过节食、健身会员资格和整形手术来改变体重。

paragraphs.sourceText: Trying to live up to the images of ''perfect" models and movie heroes has a dark side, anxiety, depression, as well as unhealthy strategies for weight loss or muscle gain. It also has a financial cost. Having an eating disorder boosts annual health care costs by nearly US$ 2,000 per person.
paragraphs.translationZh: 试图实现“完美”模特和电影英雄的形象会带来阴暗面、焦虑、抑郁，以及不健康的减肥或增肌策略。这也会带来经济成本。饮食失调会导致每人每年增加近 2,000 美元的医疗费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why is there both external and internal pressure to look "perfect"? One reason is that society rewards people who are thin and healthy-looking. Researchers have shown that body mass index is related to wages and income. Especially for women, there is a clear penalty at work for being overweight or obese. Some studies have also found an impact for men, though a less noticeable one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么有外部和内部的压力让自己看起来“完美”？原因之一是社会奖励那些苗条、看起来健康的人。研究人员表明，体重指数与工资和收入有关。特别是对于女性来说，超重或肥胖在工作中会受到明显的惩罚。一些研究也发现了对男性的影响，尽管不太明显。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the research literature is clear that labor market success is partly based on how employers and customers perceive your body image, no one had explored the other side of the question. Does a person's own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace?
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然研究文献清楚地表明，劳动力市场的成功部分取决于雇主和客户如何看待你的身体形象，但没有人探索过问题的另一面。一个人自己对身体形象的看法对收入和工作场所成功的其他指标有影响吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: Our recently published study answered this question by tracking a large national random sample of Americans over a critical time period when bodies change from teenage shape into adult form and when people build their identities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们最近发表的研究通过跟踪美国人在身体从青少年形态转变为成年人形态以及人们建立身份的关键时期的大量全国随机样本来回答这个问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: As in other research, women in our sample tend to over-perceive their weight-they think they're heavier than they are-while men tend to under-perceive theirs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与其他研究一样，我们样本中的女性倾向于过度感知自己的体重——她们认为自己比实际体重更重——而男性则倾向于低估自己的体重。

paragraphs.sourceText: We found no relationship between the average person's self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes, although self-perceived weight can influence self-esteem (自尊心), mental health and health behaviors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们发现，普通人对体重的自我感知与劳动力市场结果之间没有关系，尽管自我感知的体重会影响自尊心、心理健康和健康行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the continued gender penalty in the tabor market is frustrating, our finding that misperceived weight does not harm workers is more heartening.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然标签市场上持续存在的性别惩罚令人沮丧，但我们发现，错误的体重认知并不会伤害工人，这一发现更令人振奋。

paragraphs.sourceText: Since employers' perception of weight is what matters in the tabor market, changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category would help. Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height. We believe expanding such protections would make the labor market more fair and efficient.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于雇主对体重的看法在标签市场中至关重要，因此修改歧视法以将体型纳入其中将有所帮助。密歇根州是唯一禁止体重和身高歧视的州。我们相信扩大此类保护将使劳动力市场更加公平和高效。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The work-life balance is dead. By this, I'm not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life, and I'm definitely not saying that you have to give up one to have the other. I also acknowledge that we have a work-life problem, but I'm arguing that the concept of balance has never been helpful, because it's too limiting. You see, our language makes a difference, and how we refer to things matters because it affects our thinking and therefore our actions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 工作与生活的平衡已经消失。在此，我并不是主张你应该放弃对充实的事业和繁荣的个人生活的追求，我也绝对不是说你必须放弃其中之一才能拥有另一个。我也承认我们存在工作与生活的问题，但我认为平衡的概念从来没有帮助，因为它限制太多。你看，我们的语言很重要，我们如何指代事物很重要，因为它影响我们的思维，从而影响我们的行动。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the minimum, most of us work because we want to be able to support ourselves, our families, and the people around us. In the ideal world, we're all doing work that we're proud of and that provides meaning and purpose to us. But even if your job doesn't give you shivers of joy each new day, working is a
paragraphs.translationZh: 至少，我们大多数人工作是因为我们希望能够养活自己、家人和周围的人。在理想的世界中，我们都在做我们引以为豪的工作，这为我们提供了意义和目标。但即使你的工作并没有让你在新的一天里充满喜悦，工作也是一种享受

paragraphs.sourceText: part of what each of us does and the contribution we make to society. When you separate work and life, it's a little bit harder to make that connection. But when you think of work as part of a full life and a complete experience, it becomes easier to see that success in one aspect often supports another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们每个人所做的事情以及我们对社会做出的贡献的一部分。当你将工作和生活分开时，建立这种联系就有点困难了。但是，当您将工作视为完整生活和完整体验的一部分时，就会更容易看到一方面的成功往往会支持另一方面。

paragraphs.sourceText: Losing your balance and falling isn't pleasant. A goal to balance suggests that things could quickly get off balance, and that causes terrible outcomes. rt's more constructive to think of solutions that continue to evolve over shifts in life and work. Rather than falling or failing, you may have good days or better days or not-so-good days. These variations are normal, and it's more useful to think of life as something that is ever evolving and changing, rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep.
paragraphs.translationZh: 失去平衡并跌倒并不令人愉快。平衡目标表明事情可能很快就会失去平衡，从而导致可怕的结果。考虑随着生活和工作的变化不断发展的解决方案更具建设性。你可能会度过美好的日子、更好的日子或不太好的日子，而不是跌倒或失败。这些变化是正常的，将生活视为不断发展和变化的事物更有用，而不是视为一个稍有失误就可能出问题的高风险企业。

paragraphs.sourceText: How we talk to ourselves matters, and how we talk about issues makes a difference. Let's bury "work-life balance" and think bigger and better about work-life fulfillment to do a little less balancing and a lot more living.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们如何与自己交谈很重要，而我们如何谈论问题也会产生影响。让我们埋葬“工作与生活的平衡”，对工作与生活的满足进行更大更好的思考，减少平衡，增加生活。
